decisions.reason: As a medium-sized German GeoIT firm with strong in-house R&D, the company is well placed to learn from and refine this close-to-core authentication service, and its move from a mention in 2023 to a dedicated page in 2024 suggests growing commitment rather than withdrawal.

The framework is close to the firm's established geospatial development capabilities and fits its standards- and platform-oriented knowledge base, but its remaining only generally mentioned on the website indicates a somewhat higher risk of later rationalisation than the more prominently presented products.

This identity and access service is highly related to the firm's enterprise integration and GIS application business, and the dedicated 2024 page with more specific positioning signals that the firm is actively developing and commercialising it.

A geodata business process consulting workshop directly builds on the firm's established consulting and training strengths, so with strong related knowledge and low implementation risk it is very likely to be retained and iterated rather than dropped.
